A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEA research and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C. The complete material supports comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment experiments on four datasets in Table 2 and segmentation and embedding ablations in Tables 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and ablations, with two revised BOBSL results in Table 2.

M1.justification: The segmentation models, SignCLIP embeddings, weighted dynamic-programming alignment, and subgroup postprocessing remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use BOBSL, How2Sign, WMT-SLT SRF, and SwissSLi for alignment. Auxiliary training resources and the BSL Corpus and isolated-sign recognition evaluations are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Original/Original+, SAT/SAT+, segmentation-model comparators, and CSLR2 gloss alternatives retain the same membership in their corresponding comparisons in Tables 2–4.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, evaluation metrics, training settings, random-search procedures, and Table 5 parameters are unchanged. No protocol revision is reported alongside the updated scores.

E4.justification: The existing BOBSL sensitivity test of initializing SEA with SAT+ subtitles has two revised scores in Table 2, updating its robustness evidence without adding a condition. The segmentation and embedding ablations and Figure 3 case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point scores without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes BOBSL F1@0.50 for 'SignCLIP-BSL + SAT+ subtitles' from 74.81 to 75.27 on validation and from 65.68 to 65.81 on test. Other scores and rankings remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain the numerical update.

T1.justification: The alignment definitions, cost function, similarity formulation, and dynamic-programming recurrence in Section 3.3 and Appendix A are identical.

C1.justification: The claims of modular, cross-language, state-of-the-art subtitle alignment and usefulness for parallel-data creation are retained. Adding 'in solving this specific problem' in the conclusion does not redefine their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of segmentation, embeddings, finetuning, and dependence on prior subtitle timing are unchanged. The limitations concerning dataset biases, irrelevant signing, and unstudied human workflows are also identical.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link and a Section 3.4 footnote explicitly locating the finetuned SignCLIP checkpoints. v1 already provides a general code repository link; implementation settings and appendix annotation instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to prior alignment and segmentation research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises institutional affiliation wording, adds resource-link text, renumbers subsequent footnotes, and lightly edits the conclusion. Section organization and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added links cause limited header, footnote, column, and page-flow adjustments, including shifts of Tables 3–4 within page 8. Figure content, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new checkpoint-specific link and project-page link make resource documentation more useful than v1's general repository link, providing a modest reproducibility benefit. The unexplained Table 2 score updates preserve rankings and do not establish stronger scientific quality; the method, analyses, and appendices otherwise remain stable.
